title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: Advanced review set explorer for KQL queries
summary: The rollout, default state, licensing background and query limits are supported. Hold because the explorer instructions omit the route to a case, and the claim that unpermissioned users cannot see the tab goes beyond the documented access prerequisite. The role-management path stops early, and audit-search permissions need to acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The explorer is a new query experience in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium) review sets.
claims.quote: We’re introducing the Advanced Review Set Explorer (public preview) for review sets in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium).

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Reviewers can use Kusto Query Language queries to filter review set content.
claims.quote: With the Advanced review set explorer (preview), you can query, filter, and visualize review set data directly in the Microsoft Purview portal without modifying the underlying content.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The explorer supports aggregation of review set data.
claims.quote: The `summarize` operator aggregates data by applying functions like `count()`, `sum()`, or `avg()`, and groups results based on specified columns.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The explorer supports pattern-based text extraction.
claims.quote: Build powerful queries with complex filtering, pattern-based text extraction, and data format parsing.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Queries can return a table or chart visualization.
claims.quote: Queries run against the full set of indexed items and return either tabular results or chart visualizations.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Existing KeyQL searching continues unchanged alongside the new KQL option.
claims.quote: Users can continue using existing KeyQL‑based searching within review set without change.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The change does not modify existing queries or workflows.
claims.quote: No existing queries or workflows are modified.

claims.claim: The route supplied for opening the explorer begins at case > Review sets > review set > Advanced review set explorer (preview).
claims.quote: Select the **eDiscovery** solution card, and then select **Cases** in the left navigation.

The current route starts inside a case without saying how to reach it. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-review-set-explorer.

claims.quote: Queries are read-only and don't modify review set content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Queries run against the current review set's indexed items rather than a new data source.
claims.quote: All queries in the Advanced review set explorer (preview) run against the current review set’s indexed items. You don't need to specify a table name. The review set acts as the default data source.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A query returning more than 10,000 results returns only the first 10,000.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Older review sets may lack KQL properties and return a column-not-found error when those properties are queried.
claims.quote: Some older review sets might not support certain KQL properties if those properties weren't available when the review set was created and data was generated. Querying an unsupported property in an older review set results in a column not found error.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn documents creating a new review set and using Add to review set to regenerate data with the latest properties.
claims.quote: To resolve this error, create a new review set and use the **Add to review set** process to regenerate the data with the latest supported properties.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding data to a review set can change the results of a previously run query.
claims.quote: Results reflect the current indexed state of the review set. If you add more data to the review set, the query might return different results.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is included within the licensing for premium eDiscovery review sets.

claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Office 365 E1, Office 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E3 users can instead receive Microsoft Purview Suite or the Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on.
claims.quote: Alternatively, users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
